title: Source-based assessment pattern and coverage model
status: Descriptive study-priority model and generated MCQ blueprint. It is not a validated exam-prediction model.

evidence.answerCompanionAuthority: Uploaded companion authorship is unverified. Primary lecture sources resolve conflicts.
evidence.scope: Only the supplied Exam 1 Review is direct question-format evidence. No actual Midterm II paper, answer-key frequency data, or held-out exam is supplied.

userRequestedAdaptation.format: Four-option A–D questions with varied option lengths, substantial sentence-length explanations, plausible misconceptions, application, and controlled-design reasoning.
userRequestedAdaptation.boundary: The source review uses written conceptual prompts rather than an A–D exam. Multiple-choice format and explicit design tasks are user-requested adaptations. Researcher-name/year dependence from PSYC301 is not treated as evidence about LING285.
userRequestedAdaptation.retained: All 80 existing written prompts retain their IDs, prompt wording, answers, and rubrics.

weightExplanation: Weights for the six observed primary patterns equal their counts among the 20 uploaded prompts. The design weight of 1 is an explicit user-requested extension, not an observed instructor-question frequency. These positive relevance weights are not normalized probabilities and do not estimate the chance a question will appear.

moduleII.futureLectures: Append a 50-question bank for each supplied later lecture. Keep the cumulative test at 100, with 50 per format, and rebalance each lecture’s contribution without deleting its quiz bank or saved work.

formatChecks: Exactly four distinct options with stable a/b/c/d IDs.
One keyed answer and independent explanatory feedback for every option.
Substantial varied choices with plausible within-topic misconceptions rather than universal-word or option-length shortcuts.
Distinct explanatory tasks and inferences rather than padding the count with superficial paraphrases.
Lecture quiz ownership is explicit. Background source links do not make the same question count in multiple lecture quizzes.

ranking.purpose: Order study questions by documented source relevance and deliberate curricular coverage, not forecast an unseen test.
inputs: Question pattern or patterns, their numeric weights, and explicit examReviewRefs when conceptually justified.
ranking.textSimilarity: A deterministic TF–IDF cosine comparison can measure lexical overlap with the 20 review prompts. Its result measures document overlap, not semantic understanding, correctness, exam probability, or the professor’s intention.
ranking.patternScore: Use the supplied positive patternWeights. For multiple patterns use their arithmetic mean so adding labels cannot automatically inflate the score.
ranking.directEvidence: Nonempty examReviewRefs link an item to specific observed reasoning demands. Empty refs mark an extension whose content is lecture-supported without a direct counterpart in the supplied review.
ranking.selection: Within the chosen module, balance the required counts by format and authoritative lecture owner, then use the documented relevance priorities within those pools. Module II primary tests contain 100 unique items, with 50 of each format. Each complete lecture quiz contains 50 unique items, with 25 of each format. Additional lectures share the same 100 test places.
ranking.audit: Store the component scores, matching review item numbers, tie-break rule, selected IDs, and model revision with any generated practice-test selection. Rankings can change when new material or actual review evidence is supplied.

limitations: Twenty review prompts are a finite, nonrandom sample. They do not reveal actual test frequencies or establish generalizable prediction accuracy.
The review demonstrates conceptual explanations, comparisons, qualitative trajectories, and representation interpretation. It provides no evidence for a researcher-name-heavy LING285 exam.
Multiple-choice performance does not replace explaining a mechanism in one’s own words. Written practice remains available.
Module II mode, boundary, perturbation, and formant questions transfer the observed reasoning style to supplied later lectures. No Midterm II exam format or content frequency is claimed.
The proposed laryngeal experiment has no supplied completed participant dataset. Its predicted outcome must not become an asserted measured result.

Corrected stiffness direction, discrete-chain frequency limits, assigned membrane frequencies, separately tuned boundary demonstrations, and source-versus-filter distinctions remain constraints on every item.
Relevance ranking is transparent study prioritization. It is not a trained or validated statistical forecast of an instructor exam.
